question: A 33-year-old woman with a history of multiple sclerosis is brought to the physician because of dizziness, urinary incontinence, loss of vision in her right eye, and numbness and weakness of the left leg. She has had recurrent episodes of neurological symptoms despite several changes in her medication regimen. An MRI of the brain shows several new enhancing lesions in the periventricular white matter and the brainstem. Treatment with a drug that binds to CD52 is initiated. Which of the following agents was most likely prescribed?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Multiple sclerosis -> neurological symptoms -> recurrent episodes despite medication changes -> new enhancing lesions on brain MRI -> drug that binds to CD52 prescribed -> Alemtuzumab -> 95%
CHAIN: CD52 binding drug -> Alemtuzumab -> used in multiple sclerosis -> targets immune cells -> reduces inflammation -> 90%
analysis: The patient's history of multiple sclerosis and the presence of new enhancing lesions on MRI suggest an active inflammatory process. The drug that binds to CD52 and is commonly used in the treatment of multiple sclerosis is Alemtuzumab.
